title: Hong and Kung's red-blue pebble game: the partition lemma and I/O lower bounds for the FFT and matrix multiplication
summary: The red-blue pebble game of Hong Jia-Wei and H. T. Kung (STOC 1981) models a computation on a directed acyclic graph run with S words of fast memory and unlimited slow memory: a red pebble on a vertex is its value held in fast memory, a blue pebble its value held in slow memory, and each load or store costs one I/O operation. This formalisation defines the game, complete calculations and the minimum I/O time Q, and proves three families of results from the paper, with explicit constants and, where the paper states one, in its asymptotic form.
